song-seed-hotrs-guitar.title: House of the Rising Sun

content.text:
[Verse 1]
Am        C         D         F
There is a house in New Orleans
Am        C     E
They call the Rising Sun
Am            C       D             F
And it's been the ruin of many a poor boy
Am       E        Am
And God, I know I'm one

[Verse 2]
Am       C         D          F
My mother was a tailor
Am           C          E
She sewed my new blue jeans
Am       C       D           F
My father was a gambling man
Am       E       Am
Down in New Orleans

[Verse 3]
Am         C          D        F
Oh mother, tell your children
Am        C           E
Not to do what I have done
Am          C        D          F
Spend your lives in sin and misery
Am           E          Am
In the house of the Rising Sun

song-seed-hotrs-guitar.notes: Arpeggiated 6/8 — the classic pattern. Traditional song, public domain.

song-seed-hotrs-drums.title: House of the Rising Sun

content.text:
time: 6/8
tempo: 228
subdivision: 1

# Intro - guitar alone; keep the 6/8 pulse with the hi-hat foot x7
HF: x - - x - -

# Pickup fill - drums enter on the last intro bar
T1: - - - o - -
T2: - - - - o -
S:  - - - - - o
K:  o - - - - -

# Verse groove - hats on every eighth, kick on 1, snare on 4 x7
HH: x x x x x x
S:  - - - o - -
K:  o - - - - -

# Verse turnaround - an extra kick pushes into the next section
HH: x x x x x x
S:  - - - o - g
K:  o - - - o -

# Organ break - move to the ride, kick on both pulses x7
RD: x x x x x x
S:  - - - o - -
K:  o - - o - -

# Break fill - walk down the toms
S:  o - o - - -
T1: - - - o - -
T2: - - - - o -
FT: - - - - - o
K:  o - - - - -

# Last verse - crash in and accent the backbeat
CR: X - - - - -
RD: x x x x x x
S:  - - - X - -
K:  o - - o - o

# ...and hold that groove x6
RD: x x x x x x
S:  - - - X - -
K:  o - - o - o

# Ending - flam the last backbeat and let the crash ring
CR: X - - - - -
S:  - - - f - -
K:  o - - - - -

song-seed-hotrs-drums.notes: Drum part for the SongBook's canonical song, so the guitar/piano/ukulele seeds have something to play against. 6/8 throughout — one cell per eighth, counted 1-2-3 4-5-6, with the kick on 1 and the snare on 4. The written 228 is the EIGHTH note (dotted quarter ~76), so start at 50-75% with the BPM control and work up. Drums sit out the 8-bar intro (hi-hat foot keeps the pulse), enter on the pickup fill, then verse groove on hats, organ break on the ride, and a flam into the final crash. 32 bars = four times through the 8-bar Am-C-D-F-Am-C-E-E progression. Traditional song, public domain.

song-seed-example-rock-beat.title: Example Rock Beat

content.text:
time: 4/4
tempo: 96
subdivision: 2

# Basic rock beat x2
HH: x x x x x x x x
S:  - - - - o - - -
K:  o - - - - - o -

# Open hats and a ghost
HH: x - o - x - o -
S:  - - - - o - - g
K:  o - - o - - o -

# Fill down the toms
S:  x - x - X - - -
T1: - - - - - x - -
T2: - - - - - - x -
FT: - - - - - - - x
K:  o - - - o - - -

# Crash and out
CR: X - - - - - - -
K:  o - - - - - - -

song-seed-example-rock-beat.notes: Worked example of the PortOS drum-grid format: two bars of a basic rock beat, a bar with open hi-hats and a ghost snare, a fill down the toms, and a crash. Practice it slower with the BPM control, then loop the fill bar.
